newsitem.title: GHANA: Blackpod disease hits secondary Ghana cocoa area.
newsitem.headline: Blackpod disease hits secondary Ghana cocoa area.

text.p: An outbreak of blackpod disease has hit cocoa in Ghana's Brong Ahafo region where about 12 percent of the country's crop is grown, the official Daily Graphic newspaper said on Tuesday.
"The incidence is causing a lot of concern among farmers as they foresee a possible loss of income in the pending main season," it said.

The areas around Bechem, Goaso and Sankore had been hit, according to the paper, but a Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) official in the regional capital Sunyani downplayed the report, saying the main October to March harvest would not be affected.
"The main crop will be under control. The rains have stopped and the farmers are now seriously spraying," Nana Yeboah Afari, regional manager for quality control, told Reuters.
Blackpod is a fungal disease that attacks pods and rots the beans inside. It can be controlled by applying copper-based chemicals.
Heavy rainfall often leads to outbreaks of the disease in the region, said a private cocoa dealer.
Its spread was hastened this year by late delivery of chemicals to farmers following changes to the distribution network by farmers' leaders, Afari said.
The COCOBOD had now stepped in to assist with deliveries, he added.
A September report by London trader ED&F Man said damp cool weather since high rainfall in July and August had led to higher levels of blackpod infection than seen in recent years.
COCOBOD data show Brong Ahafo produced 36,585 tonnes of cocoa in 1992/93, 12 percent of the 305,724-tonne national crop.
Afari would not say how much came from the region last year. Most cocoa of Ghana's is grown in the country's Western region.
Ghana's 1995/96 production was estimated at 400,000 tonnes, Finance Minister Kwame Peprah said last week.
The ED&F Man report put the figure at 390,000 tonnes.
